gettingStarted.title: Getting started: a kanban board in your Discord server
gettingStarted.description: Set up KanbanCord in a few minutes: add the bot, create a board, and add and move tasks with slash commands, without leaving Discord.
gettingStarted.summary: Add the bot, create your first board and your first tasks.
gettingStarted.intro: KanbanCord gives your Discord server kanban boards: a simple, visual way to track tasks as they move from “to do” to “done”. Think of a board as your team's to-do list, split into stages, that everyone in the server can see and update. You set it up and use it with slash commands, right where your community already talks.
gettingStarted.addTitle: 1. Add the bot to your server
gettingStarted.add: Use Add to Discord on this page or at the bottom of any page, and choose your server. You need the Manage Server permission there. The bot follows your server's roles from the start, so there is nothing else to set up.
gettingStarted.boardPermission: Creating boards needs the Manage Server permission by default; everyone who can send messages can then add and move tasks. See <permissions>roles and permissions</permissions> for the details.
gettingStarted.columns: The new board has three columns: To Do, In Progress and Done. Change them whenever you like with /column add, /column rename, /column move and /column delete. Many teams add a Review or Blocked column.
gettingStarted.boardAlt: A KanbanCord board named Game Jam 2026 with five columns: Backlog, To Do, In Progress, Review and Done. Each task shows its labels, priority and the people assigned.
gettingStarted.boardCaption: A board with a few columns added, as the website shows it. In Discord, /board view shows the same board.
gettingStarted.tasks: /task create board:Sprint opens a short form for the task's title and description. If your server uses assignees, due dates or priorities, the form asks for those too. Typing a board or task name in any command suggests matches as you type.
gettingStarted.fromMessage: Someone said something that should be on the board? Long-press or right-click the message, then Apps → Create task. A short message becomes the title; a longer one goes in the description. Either way the task links back to the message, and you can change everything before it is saved.
gettingStarted.move: As work progresses, move tasks across the board with /task move, for example to Done to tick them off your to-do list. /task view shows a task in full, with a menu for everything you may do to it: edit, move, assign, set a due date, comment, follow or delete.
gettingStarted.view: /board view shows the whole board, and /board list every board in the server.
gettingStarted.featuresTitle: 5. Choose what your tasks can have
gettingStarted.features: New servers start in simple mode: boards, columns, and tasks with a title and a description. That is often all a small to-do list needs. When you want more, a server manager can switch on assignees, due dates with reminders, priorities, labels, comments and custom permissions with /kanbancord features. Switching one off again hides it without deleting anything.
gettingStarted.post: Run /board post in a channel to post the whole board as one message that updates itself whenever anything changes. See board posts and update feeds for the other ways to keep your team up to date.
gettingStarted.next: Run /guide in Discord for these steps with your progress ticked off, and /help for every command with examples. The website shows every board at a glance, with drag and drop, whenever you want the big picture.

toDoList.title: A shared to-do list for your Discord server
toDoList.description: Keep a to-do list in Discord that your whole server can see and update: add tasks, tick them off, and see what is left at a glance.
toDoList.summary: A todo list everyone in the server can see, update and tick off.
toDoList.intro: Most Discord servers keep their to-do list somewhere: a pinned message someone has to edit, a spreadsheet, or just scattered in chat. KanbanCord keeps it in your server as a shared todo list that everyone can see and update, stays current by itself, and never needs a single person to maintain it.
toDoList.stages: A KanbanCord board is a to-do list split into columns. New boards start with To Do, In Progress and Done: add tasks to To Do, move them along as someone works on them, and ticking one off means moving it to Done. You can see at a glance what is left, what is being worked on and what is finished. This way of working is called kanban, but you do not need to know the word to use it.
toDoList.checklist: Want a plain checklist instead? Keep just two columns, To Do and Done, with /column delete. Or keep a checklist inside a single task: on the website, a task's description can hold tick boxes.
toDoList.taskAlt: A task open on the website, with a checklist in its description: two items ticked, two still to do.
toDoList.taskCaption: A checklist inside a task. Tick items off right in the task's description.
toDoList.setupTitle: Set it up in a minute
setup: /board post board:To-do in the channel where it should live posts the whole list as one message.
Anyone can press Add task on that message to add something, or use /task create.
toDoList.post: The post edits itself whenever the list changes, from Discord or the website, so the channel always shows the current state. Pin it, and it works like a to-do list pinned at the top of the channel that nobody has to keep up to date. It pings nobody, and several lists can share a channel.
toDoList.tick: Pick a task from the post's menu to open it privately, then move it to Done. Or run /task move task:... column:Done. If your server has an update feed with buttons, each update shows a button per column, so ticking a task off is one click.
toDoList.shared: A board belongs to the server, not to one person, and it follows your Discord roles: everyone who should see it can, and you decide who may change it. That makes it a good fit for a team's tasks, a community's event planning, a game server's build list, or a study group's assignments.
toDoList.moreTitle: When a to-do list is not enough
toDoList.more: Switch on more with /kanbancord features as your needs grow: assign tasks to people, give them due dates with reminders, sort them with labels and priorities, and discuss them in comments. Until then, simple mode keeps your list simple.

assignTasks.title: Assigning tasks and sharing work in Discord
assignTasks.description: Assign tasks to people or whole Discord roles, so everyone knows who is doing what, and the right people hear about their tasks.
assignTasks.summary: Give tasks to people or roles, and keep them in the loop.
assignTasks.intro: A shared task list works best when everyone knows who is doing what. KanbanCord lets you assign tasks to people and to whole Discord roles, shows who is on each task, and tells people about the tasks they are assigned to.
assignTasks.switch: Assigning is one of the features servers switch on when they need it. A server manager runs /kanbancord features and picks Assignees.
assign: /task assign board:Sprint task:Fix login assigns you.
/task assign task:Fix login user:@Mia assigns someone else.
/task assign task:Fix login role:@Design assigns a whole role, so the task is for the team rather than one person. Assigning a role only says who the task is for; it gives the role no extra rights.
/task unassign takes someone off, with the same options.
assignTasks.elsewhere: You can also pick people when you create a task, since the form asks for them once assignees are on, and from the task's menu in /task view. On an update feed with buttons, every post has a picker showing who is assigned: add or remove people right there.
assignTasks.panelAlt: The task panel on the website showing a task assigned to two people, Alex and Theo, and to the Programmers role, with its priority, due date and labels.
assignTasks.panelCaption: A task assigned to two people and a whole role.
assignTasks.loop: People hear about the tasks they are assigned to by direct message: when they are assigned, when the task moves, when its due date changes, when someone comments, and more. Everyone chooses what they get with /notifications, and nobody is ever told about their own changes. If an update feed already mentioned someone in a channel they can see, they can skip the direct message about the same thing.
assignTasks.follow: Not assigned, but want to keep an eye on a task? Follow it from its menu, from the website, or with the Follow button on a feed post, and you will hear about it like its assignees do.
assignTasks.who: By default, everyone who can send messages may assign themselves, and moderators (Manage Messages) may assign others. Servers can change that, per board and per role; see <permissions>roles and permissions</permissions>.

dueDates.title: Due dates and reminders in Discord
dueDates.description: Give tasks due dates and let KanbanCord remind the people on them by direct message, a day before and when a task is overdue.
dueDates.summary: Deadlines, and reminders before they pass.
dueDates.intro: Deadlines slip when nobody sees them coming. KanbanCord gives tasks due dates and reminds the people on them by direct message before a task is due and when it is overdue, so your to-do list does not quietly fall behind.
dueDates.switch: A server manager runs /kanbancord features and picks Due dates. Boards can switch it off again for themselves on the website.
dueDates.set: When you create a task, the form asks when it is due. For an existing task:
dueDates.when: when understands today, tomorrow, in 3 days, in 2 weeks, in 5 hours, or a date like 2026-10-01 or 2026-10-01 17:00. A date alone is due at the end of that day. Use none to remove the due date. Times you type in Discord are in UTC; Discord then shows every due date in each reader's own time zone, and on the website you pick dates in your own.
dueDates.reminders: The people on a task get a direct message when it is due within a day, and again once it is overdue. Each reminder is sent once per due date: change the date, and the reminders start over. Tasks in a board's last column count as done and get no reminders.
dueDates.who: Who is reminded? Everyone who hears about the task: the people assigned to it, whoever created it, and anyone following it. Each person can turn reminders off with the rest of their direct messages in /notifications, or on the website.
dueDates.feed: An <postsFeeds>update feed</postsFeeds> can post reminders in a channel too, mentioning the people on the task. They are off in new feeds; switch them on in the feed's settings on the website.
dueDates.seeing: Task lists in Discord show each task's due date as “in 2 days” or “3 hours ago”. On the website, filter a board to overdue tasks or those due in the next seven days.
dueDates.filterAlt: A board filtered to tasks due in the next seven days: six of fourteen tasks are shown.
dueDates.filterCaption: The board filtered to what is due this week.

labelsPriorities.title: Organising tasks with labels and priorities
labelsPriorities.description: Sort tasks with coloured labels and priority levels, created and applied with slash commands in Discord, and filter by them on the website.
labelsPriorities.summary: Coloured labels and priority levels to sort your tasks.
labelsPriorities.intro: As a task list grows, you want to see at a glance what kind of work each task is and what matters most. Labels and priorities do that, and both are managed with slash commands.
labelsPriorities.switch: A server manager runs /kanbancord features and picks Labels, Priorities or both. Each board has its own labels and priority levels.
labelsPriorities.priorities: Boards start with five levels, from most to least urgent: Critical, High, Medium, Low and Ignorable. Set a task's level with /task priority, or pick it in the form when you create the task.
priorityCommands: /priority list board:Sprint shows the levels and how many tasks have each.
/priority create name:Urgent color:Red position:1 adds a level; position 1 is the most urgent.
/priority move reorders them, /priority edit renames or recolours one, and /priority delete removes one (tasks that had it are left without a priority).
labelsPriorities.labels: Labels say what a task is about: Bug, Design, Event, Docs. A task can have several.
labelCommands: /label create board:Sprint name:Bug color:Red makes one. Pick a colour from the list or type any hex colour; leave it out and the board's least used colour is chosen.
/task label task:Fix login label:Bug puts it on a task, and the same command takes it off again.
/label list, /label edit and /label delete manage them.
labelsPriorities.filter: On the <website>website</website>, a board's search bar filters tasks by label, by priority, by who is assigned and by due date, so “every high-priority bug” is two clicks away.
labelsPriorities.filterAlt: A board filtered to tasks with the Code label, showing each task with its coloured labels and priority badge.
labelsPriorities.filterCaption: Every task labelled Code, with its priority on the right.

postsFeeds.title: Keeping your team up to date: board posts and update feeds
postsFeeds.description: Show where things stand with a live board post that updates itself, or follow every change with an update feed that pings the right people.
postsFeeds.summary: A live board in a channel, or a post for every change.
postsFeeds.intro: A task list only helps if people look at it. KanbanCord can show your boards in your channels in two ways. Most servers use one of them; they also work well together.
postsFeeds.posts: /board post board:Sprint posts the whole board in the channel or thread you run it in, as a single message: every column with its tasks. Whenever anything on the board changes, from Discord or the website, the message edits itself a moment later. It works like a live dashboard, or a to-do list pinned to the top of the channel that is always current.
postPoints: It pings nobody: it is there when people want to look.
Anyone can open a column or a task from it, or press Add task. What opens is only visible to them and uses their own permissions, so one person's clicks never change the post for everyone.
If some people in the channel could not normally see the board, you are asked before posting. In a private thread, only its members count.
To stop a post, delete its message.
postsFeeds.feeds: /kanbancord feed channel:#updates (for server managers) posts a message for each change: a task created, moved, assigned, commented on, and so on, mentioning the people it concerns. Its posts can show the whole task with buttons to act on it right there, and each task can get its own thread for discussion.
postsFeeds.feedsMore: Setting feeds up, choosing what they post and who they mention, giving tasks threads, and what to check when something does not show up are all in <feedsThreads>update feeds and task threads</feedsThreads>.
postsFeeds.which: Use a board post when people mostly want to know where things stand: a small team, a shared to-do list, an event checklist. Use a feed when people need to know when something changes, especially when it concerns them. Busy servers often do both: a board post in #board and a feed in #updates.
postsFeeds.audit: For a complete record, /kanbancord audit-channel channel:#kanban-log mirrors the audit log: every change, compactly, pinging nobody. The full audit log, with filters, is on the website.
postsFeeds.dm: Besides channels, people get direct messages about tasks they are assigned to, created or follow. See assigning tasks and /notifications.

feedsThreads.title: Update feeds and task threads in Discord: set up, fine-tune and fix
feedsThreads.description: Post every change to your Discord channels with update feeds, choose what they post and who they mention, give each task its own thread, and fix what does not show up.
feedsThreads.summary: Feeds, mentions and a thread per task, step by step.
feedsThreads.intro: An update feed posts in a channel every time something happens on your boards, and mentions the people it concerns. A board can also give each task its own thread for discussion. This guide sets both up step by step, explains every setting, and lists what to check when something does not show up. Everything here can be done in Discord; the website has the same settings if you prefer it.
feedsThreads.add: A server manager runs /kanbancord feed channel:#updates. Add board:Sprint to cover one board; leave it out to cover every board, including boards made later.
addPoints: The bot needs View Channel and Send Messages in that channel. If it is missing either, the command says so and saves nothing.

A new feed posts most events: tasks created, changed, moved and deleted, people and roles assigned, new comments, labels, and changes to columns and boards. It mentions people when they are assigned or unassigned. Due date reminders, edited and deleted comments and board settings are off until you switch them on. Press Choose events and mentions on the reply to change any of it straight away.
Running the command again for the same channel and board updates that feed instead of adding a second one.
Posts are interactive by default: under each update, the whole task, with buttons to move it, assign people, edit or follow it. Add interactive:False for short posts without buttons.
feedsThreads.chooseTitle: 2. Choose what it posts and who it mentions
feedsThreads.choose: /kanbancord settings lists the server's feeds. Pick one from the menu to open its editor, where each menu saves as you change it:
choosePoints: What it posts: every event, from tasks created, moved and renamed to comments, labels, due date reminders and changes to the board itself.

Which posts mention the people involved. Who that is depends on the event: someone being assigned or unassigned mentions that person; anything else about a task mentions the people assigned to it. Nobody is ever mentioned about a change they made themselves.
Which boards it covers: every board, or the ones you pick.
Posts with or without buttons, and whether roles assigned to a task are mentioned too, besides people.
Delete feed, which asks first. Posts already in the channel stay.
feedsThreads.grouped: Quick changes to the same task are grouped into one post, so moving a task and assigning someone a moment later is one message, not two.
feedsThreads.feedsAlt: An update feed's settings on the website: the channel, its board, and for each kind of change whether it is posted and whether it mentions people.
feedsThreads.feedsCaption: The same settings on the website, in Server settings → Notifications.
several: A server can have as many feeds as it likes: one for every board in #updates, plus one for the Design board in #design, say. A change is posted by every feed that covers its board.
Feeds in the same channel are posted there once, with everything either of them wants, so a channel never gets the same update twice.
feedsThreads.board: A feed covering many boards can treat one of them differently: post fewer events about a busy board, or mention nobody about a quiet one. Whoever may edit the board runs /board notifications board:Sprint, picks the feed, and changes its menus. Only that board is affected.
boardPoints: The board follows the feed's own settings until something is changed here.
Use the feed's settings undoes the board's changes. Choosing the same as the feed does that too, for that event.
The feed's editor in /kanbancord settings does not show a board's changes; on the website, the feed lists the boards that changed it.
feedsThreads.threads: A board with a feed can give each task its own thread in that feed's channel, so the discussion about a task stays with the task instead of scrolling past in chat. Whoever may edit the board switches it on:
threadPoints: Which channel: threads go in one of the board's feed channels. With only one, it is chosen for you; with several, add channel:#updates. No feed for the board yet? Add one first (step 1).

Public or private: public by default, started from the task's post in the channel, so anyone in the channel can join. With private:True, only the task's creator and assignees are in it (and Discord's server moderators, who can see every thread). New assignees are added as they are assigned. Private threads need a text channel; announcement channels only have public threads.

Where updates go once a task has its thread: by default to both the thread and the channel, and only the channel post mentions people, so nobody is pinged twice. updates:Only the thread keeps the channel to new tasks only, with everything after that in each task's thread. updates:Only the channel posts nothing in threads, leaving them for discussion.
Permissions: the bot needs Create Public Threads (or Create Private Threads) and Send Messages in Threads in the channel. The command tells you which is missing.
behave: A task gets its thread the first time something happens to it after threads are switched on, so existing tasks get one too, as they are worked on. To start one straight away, press Discuss in thread on the task, in /task view or under a feed post; once the thread exists, the button opens it.

On a board with a feed but threads switched off, Discuss in thread tells people threads are off. Whoever may edit the board is offered to switch them on instead, in the board's feed channel (or one they pick, if there are several).
The thread is renamed when the task is, and archived when the task is deleted or archived.
Updates posted in the thread include new comments made in KanbanCord, if the feed posts comments. Messages written in the thread stay in Discord: they are not copied into the task.
If someone deletes a task's thread, the task gets a new one the next time something happens to it.
Switching threads off stops new threads; existing ones stay as they are, and still close when their task is deleted.
feedsThreads.showSetting: /board threads board:Sprint on its own shows the board's setting. Options you leave out keep their current value, so /board threads board:Sprint updates:Only the thread changes just that.
where: Add a feed: /kanbancord feed, or Server settings → Notifications on the website.
A feed's events, mentions, boards, buttons, or deleting it: /kanbancord settings → pick the feed, or Server settings → Notifications.
A feed's events and mentions for one board: /board notifications, or the board's settings → Notifications.
Task threads: /board threads, or the board's settings → Task threads.
What you are told by direct message: /notifications, or Settings → Notifications. Every direct message also has a button to stop messages from its server.
The audit log channel, every change pinging nobody: /kanbancord audit-channel.
feedsThreads.whoChanges: Adding feeds, changing them and the audit log channel are for server managers. A board's own feed settings and its threads are for whoever may edit that board.
setups: One channel for everything: a feed for every board in #updates. Simple, and fine for small servers.
A channel per team: a feed per board in each team's own channel, so each team only sees its own work.
A quiet channel, discussion in threads: a feed with threads on and updates going only to the thread. The channel shows each new task once; everything after happens in its thread.
Sensitive tasks: a separate board with private threads, in a channel only its team can see.
Feed and board post together: a board post in #board for where things stand, and a feed in #updates for what just happened.
feedsThreads.fixTitle: When something does not show up
feedsThreads.nothingTitle: Nothing is posted in the channel
nothing: Does the feed post that event? Check it in /kanbancord settings, and the board's own settings in /board notifications.
Does the feed cover that board?
Can the bot still post there? Someone may have changed the channel's permissions since the feed was added. The website marks channels the bot cannot post in.
With threads on and updates going only to the thread, later updates are in the task's thread, not the channel.
mention: Does the feed mention people for that event? The second menu in the feed's editor.
Was it their own change? Nobody is mentioned about their own changes.
Are they assigned to the task? Apart from someone being assigned or unassigned, posts mention the task's assignees.
noThread: Has something happened to the task since threads were switched on? Threads are made then, not all at once. Press Discuss in thread on the task to make it now.
Does /board threads say On, but not working? The channel no longer has a feed for this board: add one, or choose another feed channel.
Can the bot make threads there? The command names the missing permission.
Private threads only show up for their members: the task's creator, its assignees, and moderators.
feedsThreads.dm: Feeds are for channels. People also get direct messages about tasks they are assigned to, created or follow, unless a post already mentioned them where they could see it. See /notifications and assigning tasks.

permissions.title: Roles and permissions: who can see and change each board
permissions.description: KanbanCord follows your Discord roles from the start. Fine-tune who can see and change each board, per role and per person, see exactly how rules combine, and check what anyone may do.
permissions.summary: Discord roles from the start, fine-tuned per board and per person, with worked examples.
permissions.intro: Your server already says who is who with Discord roles. KanbanCord uses them, so the right people see and change the right boards from the moment you add the bot, and you can fine-tune it when you need to. This guide covers the defaults, how rules are added, and exactly how KanbanCord decides, with examples for each case.
permissions.defaults: What someone may do follows the Discord permissions their roles give them, each step adding to the one before:
defaultPoints: View Channels: see boards and their tasks.
Send Messages: also create and move tasks, comment, put labels on tasks, and assign themselves.
Manage Messages (moderators): also edit and delete tasks, and assign other people.
Manage Channels: also manage a board's columns, labels, priority levels, details and permissions, post boards in channels, and read the audit log.
View Audit Log: see boards and read the audit log.
Manage Server: everything above, plus creating and deleting boards and the server's features and permissions.
Administrator and the server owner: everything, always.
permissions.followsRoles: Nothing needs setting up, and when someone gets or loses a role in Discord, KanbanCord follows straight away.
permissions.fineTune: To change who may do what, a server manager switches on Custom permissions with /kanbancord features. Then, on the website:
fineTunePoints: Server-wide rules say what each role may do on every board: create tasks, move them, assign others, delete, manage columns and more. The defaults above are rules too, one per Discord permission, and can be changed like any other.
Board rules change that for one board, for example to make a board only visible to a Staff role.
Per-person rules make exceptions for one member, whatever their roles.
permissions.rulesAlt: The server's permission rules on the website: what each Discord permission allows, from View Channel to Manage Server, plus a rule for the Organisers role.
permissions.rulesCaption: The defaults, grouped by Discord permission, and a rule added for one role.
permissions.allowDeny: Each rule either allows or denies one thing. People who may change permissions cannot give out more than they have themselves, and nobody can take away their own right to manage the server's permissions.
permissions.switchOff: Switching custom permissions off again puts the defaults back in charge straight away. Your rules are kept, unused, and apply again when you switch it back on.
permissions.decide: Every time someone does something, KanbanCord answers one question: may this person do this, here?
permissions.decideAdmins: Administrators and the server owner may do everything. Nothing else is checked.
permissions.decideOpen: Open permissions, if the server has them on: everyone who can view channels and send messages may work with boards, columns, labels and tasks, whatever the rules say. Managing the server, board permissions, deleting or archiving boards and the audit log still go by the rules.
permissions.decideSteps: Otherwise, the rules are read in six steps. Each step that has a rule for this person and this action replaces the answer so far, so the last step with a matching rule decides:
steps: Server-wide rules for Discord permissions (the defaults)
The board's rules for Discord permissions
The board's rules for the person
permissions.decideDeny: Within one step, a Deny beats any Allow. Someone with two roles, one allowed and one denied, is denied.
permissions.decideNone: If no rule matches at all, the answer is no.
permissions.order: So a person beats their roles, roles beat Discord permissions, and a board beats the server. Note what that means for the board: any board rule outweighs every server-wide rule, even a server-wide rule for one person.
permissions.examples: The examples use a server with these roles: @everyone (View Channels), Members (Send Messages), Mods (Manage Messages) and a few roles with no Discord permissions of their own. Sam has Members.
permissions.defaultsOnly: Sam may create a task: Send Messages allows it. Sam may not edit someone else's task: nothing Sam has allows it, so the answer is no.
permissions.twoRoles: Server-wide, Helpers are allowed to delete tasks and On break is denied it. Sam has both. Both are role rules, in the same step, so the Deny wins: Sam may not delete tasks. The same goes for @everyone: a Deny for @everyone outweighs an Allow for any other role in that step.
permissions.roleVsPermissionTitle: A role rule against a Discord permission
permissions.roleVsPermission: Mods may delete tasks through Manage Messages. A server-wide rule denies deleting tasks to Trial mods. A mod who also has Trial mods may not delete tasks: role rules come after Discord permissions. It works the other way too: allow editing tasks for Artists, and every artist may edit tasks, without Manage Messages.
permissions.denyPermissionTitle: A Deny for a Discord permission
permissions.denyPermission: Deny creating tasks for everyone with View Channels, and you deny it to nearly everyone, mods included: in that step a Deny beats the Allow from Send Messages or Manage Messages. To stop one group, deny it to their role instead.
permissions.person: On break is denied creating tasks, and Sam has On break. A rule allowing Sam personally to create tasks wins: rules for a person come after rules for roles.
permissions.private: On the board Staff room: deny seeing the board to everyone with View Channels, and allow it for Staff. Everyone without Staff no longer sees it, and Staff do. Even Sam, who has a server-wide rule allowing them to see boards, cannot see it: the board's rule for View Channels comes after every server-wide rule. To let Sam in, add a rule for Sam on that board.
permissions.oneBoardTitle: Denied server-wide, allowed on one board
permissions.oneBoard: Members are denied creating tasks server-wide, and the board Suggestions allows it for Members. Sam may create tasks on Suggestions and nowhere else.
permissions.admins: Anyone with Administrator, and the server owner, may do everything on every board. No rule can change that, so the server can never lock out the people who run it.
permissions.open: With open permissions on, Sam may create columns and edit anyone's task even though no rule allows it, but still may not delete boards or read the audit log. Someone who cannot send messages is not included. Open permissions and custom permissions cannot be on together.
permissions.customOff: The server's own rules and every board's rules are set aside, and only the defaults apply. A board that was private is visible again to everyone with View Channels, so make sure that is what you want before switching it off.
permissions.left: They no longer have roles or Discord permissions here, so only rules for them personally count. With none, they may do nothing.
permissions.check: Not sure what someone may do? Check access, in the server's settings on the website, shows it for any member: every action, allowed or denied, and the rule that decided it. Start from a member and add or remove roles to see what would change, or check a set of roles on its own. In a board's settings, the same check shows what applies on that board. Server managers can check anyone, and people who may edit a board's permissions can check anyone on that board.
permissions.discord: The bot uses the same rules as the website: everything a command does is checked as the person who ran it. Buttons are shown to everyone, and if you are not allowed to use one, the bot tells you when you try. Autocomplete only suggests the boards you can see.
permissions.boardPost: One thing to keep in mind: a <postsFeeds>board post</postsFeeds> shows a board to everyone who can see its channel. Posting needs the right to edit the board, and you are asked first if some people there could not see it otherwise.
permissions.track: Every change, including changes to permissions and switching features on or off, is recorded in the audit log on the website, with who made it and whether it came from Discord or the website.

website.title: The website: every board at a glance
website.description: The KanbanCord website shows whole boards with drag and drop, search and filters, checklists, images and videos, all live with Discord.
website.summary: Drag and drop, search, filters and more, live with Discord.
website.intro: You can run KanbanCord entirely from Discord. The website is there for when you want the whole picture: every column and task of a board on one screen, and the settings that are easier with a bit of room. Sign in with Discord and pick your server.
website.dashboardAlt: The KanbanCord dashboard for a server named Pixel Forge, listing its boards: Game Jam 2026, Community Events and Website Redesign.
website.dashboardCaption: Your server's boards, after signing in.
board: Drag and drop tasks between columns and within them, and reorder the columns themselves.
Live: changes made by anyone, on the website or in Discord, appear straight away for everyone with the board open.
Search and filters: press / to search titles and descriptions, and filter by who is assigned, label, priority or due date. Filters are in the page's address, so you can share a filtered view.
website.filtersAlt: A board with its filters open: people, label, priority and due date, with six of fourteen tasks shown.
website.filtersCaption: Search and filters, right in the board's title bar.
website.tasks: Open a task to see and edit everything about it:
taskPoints: A description with formatting, and checklists you can tick off right in the task.
Images and videos, uploaded, dropped or pasted straight into the description.
People and roles, labels, priority and due date, as your server has them switched on.
Comments, and a Follow button to hear about the task by direct message.
website.taskAlt: A task open beside the board, with its priority, due date, a checklist, labels, people, roles and comments.
website.taskCaption: A task in full, beside the board.
settings: Features: which ones the server uses, and which each board switches off for itself.
Permissions: who may do what, per role, per board and per person. See roles and permissions.
Notifications: update feeds, with each event and its mentions, and your own direct messages.
Labels and priority levels for each board.
Appearance: themes, including light and dark, and accessibility options.
website.audit: Every change is recorded, newest first: who did what, when, and whether it came from Discord or the website. Filter it by board, person or kind of change.
